automation_name: AI Security Wiki Topic News Collector

cutoff_window.rule: Only public records with a visible, precise publication or update timestamp strictly inside this two-day window are retained.

source_method: Public NVD CVE API time-window discovery and direct record verification; public web search was used for supplemental discovery only. No private, proprietary, sensitive, PII, or company-internal local content was sent externally.
searched_topics: agent and tool security including MCP plugins browsers delegated authority and autonomous action
identity authentication authorization credentials and least privilege
model dataset dependency artifact runtime cloud hardware and deployment supply chains
threat modeling red teaming security evaluation assurance monitoring and release gates
AI security standards regulation governance audit evidence risk management and public incidents

qualifying_findings.summary: open 7.2.0 before 11.0.0 passes crafted OAuth authorization-endpoint URLs, including ones served by malicious MCP servers, to PowerShell such that a subexpression can execute code on Windows or WSL.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: open 7.2.0 before 11.0.0; MCP-provided OAuth endpoint to local PowerShell boundary.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Agent tool integrations must treat remote authorization metadata as untrusted and avoid passing it through shell interpreters.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: open and MCP product background are upstream-owned by ai-wiki; retain the local security boundary around untrusted authorization metadata.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: Confirm the upstream release remediation and audit developer environments using open before 11.0.0.

qualifying_findings.summary: Agno through 3.1.11 lets model-controlled function names reach PandasTools getattr(), allowing prompt injection to invoke unsafe readers such as read_pickle for code execution or local-file reads.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Agno through 3.1.11; model-selected PandasTools function-dispatch boundary.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Tool dispatch chosen from model output needs a fixed allowlist and typed argument validation rather than open reflection.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: Agno framework background is upstream-owned by ai-wiki; retain the local model-to-tool authorization implication.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: Confirm the maintainer fix and identify deployments that expose PandasTools to untrusted prompt-derived instructions.

qualifying_findings.summary: Crawl4AI 0.9.0 before 0.9.5 accepts an unfiltered CosineStrategy model_name in Docker API bodies, letting authenticated clients select a malicious Hugging Face pickle-weight repository for code execution on PyTorch below 2.6 or exhaust resources.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Crawl4AI 0.9.0 before 0.9.5; Docker API model-selection and model-artifact loading boundary.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Model identifiers are supply-chain inputs; a server must restrict repository selection and safely load artifacts.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: Crawl4AI and Hugging Face product background are upstream-owned by ai-wiki; retain the local model-artifact trust boundary.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: Verify the fixed release and review API callers that can select model repositories.

qualifying_findings.summary: Kubeflow Pipelines before 2.18.0 does not confine a requested volume-artifact path, allowing a caller who can reach the route and knows a mounted volume to read accessible files outside that volume.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Kubeflow Pipelines before 2.18.0; volume artifact GET path-containment boundary.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: ML workflow artifacts may share hosts with sensitive pipeline inputs, model outputs, and credentials; path normalization must preserve volume isolation.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: Kubeflow product background is upstream-owned by ai-wiki; retain the local artifact-read containment implication.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: Upgrade to 2.18.0 and assess exposed artifact routes and mounted-volume permissions.

qualifying_findings.summary: Kubeflow Pipelines before 2.18.0 retrieves run logs without authorizing the caller against the selected run and accepts a caller-selected pod name in the live-log path, exposing other workload logs.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Kubeflow Pipelines before 2.18.0; run/node log authorization boundary.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Pipeline logs commonly contain sensitive training, inference, and connector context; authentication at ingress is not run-level authorization.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: Kubeflow product background is upstream-owned by ai-wiki; retain the local tenant-scoped observability implication.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: Upgrade to 2.18.0 and review backend reachability, log retention, and exposure of run identifiers.

qualifying_findings.summary: Kubeflow Pipelines 0.5.1 through 2.17.0 does not authorize the requested namespace on frontend artifact routes, allowing a reachable user to read another tenant's datasets, models, or pipeline outputs when locations are known.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Kubeflow Pipelines 0.5.1 through 2.17.0; frontend artifact namespace authorization boundary.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Artifacts carry high-value model, dataset, and output data; namespace selection must be bound to the authenticated principal.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: Kubeflow product background is upstream-owned by ai-wiki; retain the local multi-tenant artifact confidentiality implication.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: Upgrade to 2.17.0 or later and review multi-user deployments that rely on Kubeflow authorization.

qualifying_findings.summary: Kubeflow Pipelines before 2.18.0 decompresses uploaded pipeline archives before namespace authorization without adequately bounding expanded data, enabling reachable callers to exhaust API-server resources.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Kubeflow Pipelines before 2.18.0; pipeline archive upload and decompression-before-authorization boundary.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Pre-authorization work must be resource-bounded so ML control planes remain available to legitimate pipelines.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: Kubeflow product background is upstream-owned by ai-wiki; retain the local availability and release-gate implication.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: Upgrade to 2.18.0 and enforce archive expansion and request-size limits at the edge.

qualifying_findings.summary: AI Engine for WordPress through 3.8.6 exposes its MCP OAuth dynamic-client-registration endpoint without authorization, allowing an attacker client and redirect URI that can obtain an administrator-approved MCP token; the consent page is also frameable for clickjacking.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: AI Engine through 3.8.6; MCP OAuth 2.1 client-registration and administrator-consent boundary.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Dynamic client registration, redirect URIs, consent, and MCP token scope jointly control delegated administrative authority.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: AI Engine product background is upstream-owned by ai-wiki; retain the local delegated-administration control implication.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: Confirm the vendor patch, rotate MCP tokens if exposed, and disable or restrict dynamic registration pending remediation.

qualifying_findings.summary: n8n before 2.42.6, 2.43.x before 2.43.3, and 3.x before 3.0.1 allows authenticated workflow authors to execute JavaScript in the main process through deprecated Function, Function Item, and LangChain Code nodes outside task-runner isolation.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: n8n affected release lines; workflow-node execution versus task-runner isolation boundary.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Agent and workflow platforms must prevent legacy code-capable nodes from bypassing execution isolation.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: n8n and LangChain product background are upstream-owned by ai-wiki; retain the local workflow execution-isolation implication.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: Upgrade to the fixed release for the deployed line and inventory hidden legacy node references in imported workflows.

qualifying_findings.summary: Zuke before 1.51.0 accepts command-form descriptors from a writable MCP registry without applying launch-host authorization, allowing a registry writer to choose a program and arguments when a run-capable caller invokes the tool.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: @zuke/core before 1.51.0; writable MCP registry descriptor to local program-launch boundary.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: MCP registry metadata is executable supply-chain input and must not define authority or confirmation text for destructive local actions.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: Zuke and MCP catalog background are upstream-owned by ai-wiki; retain the local registry-trust and command-authority implication.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: Upgrade to 1.51.0 and restrict write access to registries consumed with --allow-run.

qualifying_findings.summary: Paperclip 2026.403.0 before 2026.416.0 permits agent API-key holders to set shell-executed cleanupCommand and teardownCommand fields on execution workspaces, yielding server-host command execution at archive time.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Paperclip 2026.403.0 before 2026.416.0; agent API-key workspace lifecycle command boundary.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Delegated agent credentials should not authorize arbitrary lifecycle hooks that execute in a server control plane.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: Paperclip product background is upstream-owned by ai-wiki; retain the local delegated lifecycle-authority implication.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: Upgrade to 2026.416.0 or later and rotate or scope agent API keys that can patch workspaces.

qualifying_findings.summary: DBHub before 0.22.6 parses double-dash comments differently from MySQL and MariaDB, letting prompt-influenced SQL hide write or DDL statements from its read-only validator while the connector executes them.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: DBHub before 0.22.6; read-only SQL validation versus MySQL/MariaDB execution boundary.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: A semantic read-only promise is unsafe when the policy parser and database parser disagree, especially where prompts can influence tool input.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: DBHub product background is upstream-owned by ai-wiki; retain the local least-privilege SQL-tool implication.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: Upgrade to 0.22.6 and ensure database credentials remain independently read-only.

qualifying_findings.summary: Flowise through 3.1.4 lets authenticated users escape vm2 and execute OS commands by using allowlisted LangChain and mammoth modules when ALLOW_BUILTIN_DEP is enabled.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Flowise through 3.1.4; custom-function sandbox and builtin-dependency allowlist boundary.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Tool and module allowlists require composition-aware testing; individually approved dependencies can still create an execution path.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: Flowise and LangChain product background are upstream-owned by ai-wiki; retain the local sandbox-assurance implication.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: Confirm the maintainer remediation and disable builtin dependencies in untrusted custom-function environments.

qualifying_findings.summary: LM Studio before 0.4.22+1 accepts backslash traversal names in model downloads, allowing a crafted model repository to plant plugin and MCP bridge configuration that launches an attacker Python payload on startup.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: LM Studio before 0.4.22+1; model-download filename to application/plugin configuration boundary.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Model supply chains can become local application supply chains when artifact extraction reaches startup-controlled files.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: LM Studio product background is upstream-owned by ai-wiki; retain the local model-artifact and plugin-persistence implication.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: Upgrade to 0.4.22+1 and inspect model and plugin configuration directories for untrusted artifacts.

qualifying_findings.summary: PDF Reader MCP 2.2.0 through before 3.0.1 reports HTTP API-key authentication as enabled but does not validate X-API-Key, leaving a default 0.0.0.0 HTTP MCP endpoint able to read any host-accessible PDF.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: @sylphx/pdf-reader-mcp 2.2.0 through before 3.0.1; HTTP MCP authentication and file-read boundary.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Misleading authentication telemetry can expose agent tools to unauthenticated callers with the server process's data access.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: PDF Reader MCP product background is upstream-owned by ai-wiki; retain the local authentication-enforcement implication.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: Upgrade to 3.0.1, bind HTTP transport narrowly, and rotate exposed API keys.

qualifying_findings.summary: praktor before 0.9.1 joins Telegram-controlled document names into its persistent agent workspace without sanitization; with the default unrestricted sender configuration, uploads can overwrite CLAUDE.md, instructions, skills, hooks, or configuration for later agent runs.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: praktor before 0.9.1; Telegram upload filename to persistent agent-workspace boundary.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: A file-write flaw becomes stored instruction injection when the destination is a durable agent context surface.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: praktor and Claude Code product background are upstream-owned by ai-wiki; retain the local persistent-instruction integrity implication.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: Upgrade to 0.9.1, restrict Telegram senders, and inspect persistent workspace instruction and hook files.

qualifying_findings.summary: Immich before 3.3.0 lets an unauthenticated caller set security-sensitive model-construction options at its machine-learning /predict endpoint, including a writable cache_dir that can be recursively removed after selected loading failures.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Immich before 3.3.0; unauthenticated ML prediction options and cache-path lifecycle boundary.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: ML service configuration should not be caller-controlled, especially when model cache maintenance can mutate mounted data.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: Immich product background is upstream-owned by ai-wiki; retain the local unauthenticated ML runtime-control implication.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: Upgrade to 3.3.0 and limit network access to the machine-learning service.

qualifying_findings.summary: RAGFlow 0.25.2 through 0.27.3 performs an OpenAI-compatible agent completion before checking whether the caller can access the requested private agent, allowing a user with a victim UUID to execute and read that workflow's output.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: RAGFlow 0.25.2 through 0.27.3; agent authorization-order boundary on chat completions.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Authorization must precede agent execution because tools can expose data or create side effects before a later denial.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: RAGFlow product background is upstream-owned by ai-wiki; retain the local private-agent authorization implication.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: Upgrade to 0.27.3 and review tenant access logs for agent UUID probing.

qualifying_findings.summary: Stirling-PDF before 3.0.0 sends attacker-controlled HTML from its AI PDF-generation agent path to WeasyPrint without the sanitizer used by the normal converter, enabling requests to internal or metadata services and embedding readable local files.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Stirling-PDF before 3.0.0; AI HTML-agent rendering boundary.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: AI-specific rendering paths must inherit the same sanitization and egress controls as conventional document conversion paths.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: Stirling-PDF product background is upstream-owned by ai-wiki; retain the local SSRF and local-file boundary implication.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: Upgrade to 3.0.0 and keep authentication enabled while evaluating any HTML-rendering agent endpoints.

qualifying_findings.summary: MoLing before 0.5.0 exposes unauthenticated SSE MCP endpoints with wildcard CORS; a malicious web page can recover the session ID from a loopback listener and send unauthorized tool calls that may reach files or commands.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: MoLing before 0.5.0 SSE mode; browser origin, session ID, and local MCP tool boundary.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Loopback binding does not protect an agent tool when browser cross-origin policy exposes session bootstrap data.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: MoLing and MCP product background are upstream-owned by ai-wiki; retain the local browser-mediated delegated-tool implication.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: Upgrade to 0.5.0 and disable SSE exposure or apply authentication and restrictive CORS.

qualifying_findings.summary: TAKO AI Agent for Okta before 3.0.1-beta exposes first-run administrator creation on all interfaces without authentication, a bootstrap token, or network restriction, letting a network attacker claim the only administrator account.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: TAKO AI Agent for Okta before 3.0.1-beta; initial administrator bootstrap boundary.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: AI administrators commonly hold synced identity data, integration credentials, and chat history; bootstrap must be single-use and protected.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: TAKO product background is upstream-owned by ai-wiki; retain the local AI-administration identity bootstrap implication.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: Upgrade to 3.0.1-beta, confirm setup completion, rotate affected secrets, and restrict the service network listener.

qualifying_findings.summary: TAKO AI Agent for Okta before 3.0.1-beta lets any authenticated user bypass AI-based Python content filtering with dynamic getattr call chains and execute arbitrary source as the application process user, root in the default container.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: TAKO AI Agent for Okta before 3.0.1-beta; authenticated React script execution and AI filtering boundary.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: AI-assisted content screening is not a substitute for a non-executable policy boundary around user-submitted code.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: TAKO product background is upstream-owned by ai-wiki; retain the local code-execution and privileged-container implication.
qualifying_findings.follow_up: Upgrade to 3.0.1-beta and rotate Okta tokens, JWT keys, and other secrets reachable by the application container.

exclusions.reason: They remain in the two-day window but were already captured in the October 29 collector artifact and subsequently synthesized; no duplicate raw record was created.
SOCFortress CoPilot findings are concrete but the product is a general security-operations platform; no independent AI-system boundary was established from the CVE descriptions for this collector.
The record references model lists but does not establish an AI-specific security boundary; excluded as ambiguous.

exclusions.candidate: CVE-2026-119656 CoreShop Agent endpoint SQL injection
exclusions.reason: Agent is an endpoint name in a general e-commerce product, not evidence of an AI system.
The October 30 CVE lacks sufficient record detail to distinguish its affected AI/MCP surface from the separately retained OAuth client-registration finding.

exclusions.candidate: CVE-2026-119339 Tesseract traineddata denial of service
exclusions.reason: The OCR model-file issue is concrete but was excluded for lower AI-system specificity relative to the retained agent, MCP, ML runtime, RAG, and model-supply-chain findings.

exclusions.candidate: General AI, MCP, and agent product announcements and pages without a security change
exclusions.reason: Excluded when they lacked a concrete vulnerability, mitigation, incident, assurance result, or precise in-window visible date.

confidence_notes: Every retained item has a precise public NVD publication timestamp inside the stated window and was checked against local October 28-29 processed collector artifacts for duplication.

NVD-first evidence establishes the public disclosure and stated affected/fixed versions but does not by itself prove deployment exposure, exploitability in a particular environment, or remediation completion.

The four Kubeflow findings share a product and release remediation but protect distinct resources: volume paths, run logs, artifact namespaces, and pre-authorization archive processing; retain that separation during ingest.
No docs/wiki or raw/processed content was changed by this collection run.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, reconcile all fixed versions and maintainer advisories or release notes before publishing operational remediation guidance.
Prioritize endpoint reachability, token rotation, and tenant-scope review for the retained MCP, agent, RAG, and identity-bound findings.
Keep broad product and framework background upstream, while synthesizing only the local security boundaries, evidence, and controls.
Split the Kubeflow and TAKO groups into their independent local security boundaries during synthesis.
